pubcol-w-b82469f4805142e7.definition_en: to harm something or cause it to work less well
pubcol-w-b82469f4805142e7.example_simple: The heavy rain did a lot of damage to the crops.
pubcol-w-b82469f4805142e7.example_complex: Repeated financial scandals have done serious damage to the bank's once-solid reputation.

pubcol-w-f8dd1984e6d146f5.definition_en: to perform physical movements or practice tasks to stay fit or improve a skill
pubcol-w-f8dd1984e6d146f5.example_simple: I do some simple exercises every morning before school.
pubcol-w-f8dd1984e6d146f5.example_complex: Her physiotherapist recommended that she do gentle strengthening exercises to speed up her recovery.

pubcol-w-5f9588f459e48b9f.definition_en: to hurt or have a bad effect on a person or thing
pubcol-w-5f9588f459e48b9f.example_simple: Eating too much sugar can do harm to your teeth.
pubcol-w-5f9588f459e48b9f.example_complex: Spreading unverified rumours online can do lasting harm to innocent people's reputations.

pubcol-w-210bfe04b1aa1a4e.definition_en: to complete school assignments at home, or to do cleaning and other tasks around the house
pubcol-w-210bfe04b1aa1a4e.example_simple: I have to do my homework before I can watch television.
pubcol-w-210bfe04b1aa1a4e.example_complex: After a long shift at work, she still had to do the housework and help the children with their homework.

pubcol-w-63c7abb370d05580.definition_en: to collect and study information about what customers want and how a market behaves
pubcol-w-63c7abb370d05580.example_simple: Before opening the café, they did some market research in the neighbourhood.
pubcol-w-63c7abb370d05580.example_complex: The start-up did detailed market research to identify a gap that larger competitors had overlooked.

pubcol-w-5ae423fd25268415.definition_en: to not feel strong dislike or hostility towards someone or something
pubcol-w-5ae423fd25268415.example_simple: I do not hate her; I just don't agree with her.
pubcol-w-5ae423fd25268415.example_complex: Despite everything that happened between them, he insists that he does not hate his former partner.

pubcol-w-93902db479bb14af.definition_en: to not do a repeated activity meant to improve a skill
pubcol-w-93902db479bb14af.example_simple: If you do not practise, you will forget how to play the piano.
pubcol-w-93902db479bb14af.example_complex: Many learners do not practise speaking regularly, which is why their fluency improves so slowly.

pubcol-w-ffdc131caf631e9a.definition_en: to carry out the tasks or responsibilities one is expected to perform
pubcol-w-ffdc131caf631e9a.example_simple: The soldier said he was only doing his duty.
pubcol-w-ffdc131caf631e9a.example_complex: She believed that voting was not merely a right but a way of doing her duty as a citizen.

pubcol-w-1d47f4be0e4e6af9.definition_en: to clean and tidy one's room
pubcol-w-1d47f4be0e4e6af9.example_simple: Please do your room before your friends come over.
pubcol-w-1d47f4be0e4e6af9.example_complex: At the small hotel, the same two staff members did all the rooms before the midday check-in.

pubcol-w-98a83c28bb0a730c.definition_en: to do something kind or helpful for someone
pubcol-w-98a83c28bb0a730c.example_simple: Could you do me a favour and close the window?
pubcol-w-98a83c28bb0a730c.example_complex: She agreed to do her neighbour a favour by watering his plants while he was away on holiday.

pubcol-w-8ab376107ae7661e.definition_en: to have a positive or beneficial effect on someone
collocations: do someone a lot of good
pubcol-w-8ab376107ae7661e.example_simple: A short walk will do you good after such a long meeting.
pubcol-w-8ab376107ae7661e.example_complex: The doctor assured him that a few weeks of rest by the sea would do him a world of good.

pubcol-w-c3d8ae8ec8b12050.definition_en: to unfairly deprive someone of something, especially by cheating or trickery
collocations: do someone out of a job
do someone out of their share
pubcol-w-c3d8ae8ec8b12050.example_simple: The salesman tried to do us out of our deposit.
pubcol-w-c3d8ae8ec8b12050.example_complex: By altering the figures, the manager effectively did several employees out of the bonuses they were owed.

pubcol-w-a4fc112fa3d00fb1.definition_en: to carry out everyday household tasks such as ironing clothes, buying groceries or washing laundry
pubcol-w-a4fc112fa3d00fb1.example_simple: On Saturdays I do the shopping and my brother does the washing.
pubcol-w-a4fc112fa3d00fb1.example_complex: They shared the chores fairly, so that whoever did the ironing was excused from doing the washing that week.

pubcol-w-8168ac8bc5f9bc43.definition_en: to behave in a deliberately polite or courteous way, often just for show
pubcol-w-8168ac8bc5f9bc43.example_simple: At the dinner he had to do the polite and chat with everyone.
pubcol-w-8168ac8bc5f9bc43.example_complex: Although she was exhausted, she did the polite for another hour, smiling at guests she barely knew.

pubcol-w-dff5e3676a433138.definition_en: used with 'could' or 'can' to say that someone needs or would like something
pubcol-w-dff5e3676a433138.example_simple: I could do with a hot cup of tea right now.
pubcol-w-dff5e3676a433138.example_complex: After such an exhausting week, the whole team could do with a proper break rather than another late meeting.

pubcol-w-580a888cb1816253.definition_en: to have a remarkably good effect or produce excellent results
pubcol-w-580a888cb1816253.example_simple: A good night's sleep can do wonders for your mood.
pubcol-w-580a888cb1816253.example_complex: The new coaching approach did wonders for a team that had seemed hopelessly out of form only months earlier.

pubcol-w-3f61333b938208d4.definition_en: to act in a way that is morally wrong or mistaken
pubcol-w-3f61333b938208d4.example_simple: He was taught never to do wrong, even when no one is watching.
pubcol-w-3f61333b938208d4.example_complex: In their eyes their hero could do no wrong, so they ignored every report of his misconduct.

pubcol-w-625a64535f28d86d.definition_en: to arrange, style or take care of your hair
pubcol-w-625a64535f28d86d.example_simple: She spent an hour doing her hair before the party.
pubcol-w-625a64535f28d86d.example_complex: He waited patiently while she did her hair, knowing they would still arrive fashionably late.

pubcol-w-0e25a06486630dd6.example_simple: My grandfather likes to do the crossword every morning.
pubcol-w-0e25a06486630dd6.example_complex: She could do the fiendishly difficult crossword in the Sunday paper faster than anyone else in the family.

pubcol-w-e2b29d83eb5271b3.definition_en: to give or perform a musical concert or recital
pubcol-w-e2b29d83eb5271b3.example_simple: The band will do a concert in the park this weekend.
pubcol-w-e2b29d83eb5271b3.example_complex: Before retiring, the pianist agreed to do one final recital in the hall where she had first performed as a child.

pubcol-w-aaf255a0b3040bf0.definition_en: to take part in a series of lessons or study on a particular subject
pubcol-w-aaf255a0b3040bf0.example_simple: I'm doing a course in web design this term.
pubcol-w-aaf255a0b3040bf0.example_complex: She decided to do an intensive course in business English before applying for jobs abroad.

pubcol-w-52af6c8a57c0fbc1.definition_en: to complete a task or piece of work that has been set, especially for study
pubcol-w-52af6c8a57c0fbc1.example_simple: I have to do an assignment on climate change for geography.
pubcol-w-52af6c8a57c0fbc1.example_complex: Rather than doing the assignment at the last minute, she planned her research over several weeks.

b47a407c-32e0-439e-a073-af2cd6c03d46.definition_en: a principle or set of beliefs laid down by an authority as unquestionably true

pubcol-w-f35cce1a9d290aaa.definition_en: to cause damage or have a harmful effect
pubcol-w-f35cce1a9d290aaa.example_simple: Too much screen time can do harm to young children.
pubcol-w-f35cce1a9d290aaa.example_complex: Well-meant but poorly planned aid can sometimes do more harm than good to local economies.

pubcol-w-e9ddc3d9a51cf085.definition_en: money paid by the state to people who are unemployed
pubcol-w-e9ddc3d9a51cf085.example_simple: After losing his job, he had to live on dole money for a few months.
pubcol-w-e9ddc3d9a51cf085.example_complex: Cuts to dole money left many families struggling to cover their basic living costs during the recession.
